editorialRule: Primary technical sources verify the stated API/implementation distinctions. Original toy examples, diagrams and design choices are explicitly marked as authored examples; they do not assert proprietary game internals.

sources.supports: Replay header/init/game/message/tracker data are distinct; a replay is not merely a video or necessarily only raw key presses.
Decoding replay data is different from obtaining/running all game rules.
Deterministic reproduction needs matching starting conditions and inputs; numerical and processing differences can break synchronization.
Simulation steps and rendering frequency need not be the same clock.
Transition and Blend Tree differ; normalized contact events should align when blending similar locomotion clips.
Root transform motion and pose evaluation have separate roles.
A modular design document can accompany a concept document; a flowchart and feature description serve related but different functions.
Normal maps change lighting normals rather than small geometric detail; Unity documents the Y+ convention.
glTF normal texture is linear tangent-space direction data, not display color.
External image content, Peter23 attribution, native dimensions and CC BY-SA 3.0 license; original used unmodified.
Small attack-delay randomness; deterministic reproduction requires matching seed/version conditions.
Global random state and InitState/state differ from independent random streams.
Graph search returns paths and is separate from locomotion and local avoidance.
Original developer describes grid subdivision and worker collision exceptions.
Pairwise physical collision setting is separate from navigation behavior.
Parallax layer scroll scale, auto scroll, and repetition have distinct roles.
Original talk metadata identifies rope simulation and taut rope challenges; full talk not claimed viewed.
Constraint projection and distance constraints in position based dynamics.
Original developer explains depth-based masking, inside-camera and overlap cases.
Height-field accumulation, capture, and rendering distinctions in the original snow presentation.
HLSL clip discards negative components; clipping does not generate a geometric cap.
Tap, hold, and slow tap interaction patterns are distinct from the gameplay action.
Acknowledgement and visibility of processing state support the next user decision.
Meaning should not depend on color alone.
Game information may use additional visual channels such as shape or labels.
Relative luminance contrast formula and its text accessibility context.
Animation Events call a function at a specified clip time; attack ownership and cleanup are authored design decisions.
Transition conditions, exit timing, and blend duration are distinct controls.
Nintendo technical disclosure maps collision/surface coordinates to paint texture and describes adjacent surface handling; not proof of every shipping game implementation.
Raycast hit UV query requires matching mesh collider conditions.
Original developer account identifies team boundary, geometry shading and submerged enemy splash readability tradeoffs; final coefficients are not disclosed.
Original author describes ray-plane interior mapping and geometry/flat texture limits.
Original Valve slides explain flow map vectors, phased layers and residual repetition/pulsing problems.
MDA distinguishes rules/data, runtime interaction and desired experience; the column uses a separate authored jump experiment.
Humanoid retargeting uses configured Avatars; authored column separates reuse from final pose/readability review.
IK poses a joint chain from an endpoint goal rather than only setting joint rotations forward.
Imported blend shapes can be driven by weights and animation keys; model and mixed-shape quality remain authored review tasks.
Clip curves can provide normalized-time data and animator parameter values; multiple clip values may blend.
Mirror is a Humanoid animation state property; this does not define every accessory, material or gameplay policy.
Official Unity case study distinguishes 24 fps artwork from 60 fps gameplay; own column tick timing is an authored model rather than recovered code.
Original developer interview describes two connected body chunks and procedural cosmetic limbs/tail.
Inertial blending stops source pose evaluation; offset decay and source Notify consequences differ from continued crossfade evaluation.
Unity fieldOfView uses vertical degrees; horizontal field depends on viewport aspect and orthographic/custom projections are distinct.
Engine conversion takes horizontal FOV and aspect ratio; own column explains which axis is fixed.
Bindings connect controls with actions; interactive rebind and binding overrides require explicit UI, saving and disposal handling.
Motion effects, camera movement and FOV should offer settings; no universal comfort value is asserted.
Game AI serves the intended player experience, with authorial control and understandable behavior. Guard rules in this column are original examples.
Original Teardown developer explains one-byte material indices, palette variations and remapping. Small 12-slot examples are authored.
Official legacy visual switching and preservation goals; detailed two-renderer architecture here is an explicitly authored model.
Erich Schaefer postmortem: component appearance variations, offline multi-direction rendering. Anchors and sorting examples are original.
2021 official explanation of 21:9 AI response issue and 19:9 limitation; toy 8/10/12 distance model is not a measured product range.
Developer describes controller direction movement with pathfinding disabled; deadzone curve and switching behavior in the column are original examples.
Position node coordinate-space distinction; grass falloff and displacement are authored and explicitly not recovered Diablo shaders.
Original developer discusses image thresholding with dither patterns and temporal stability. The 4x4 exercise is a separate teaching model.
Direct Matt Stark interview: many meshes modified within a frame, mesh slicing optimization. Plane clipping derivation and tests are original illustrative exercises.
Original demo implements camera/traveller transformations, finite recursion and clipping. Authored teaching formula states its own half-turn axis convention; not Valve code.
Stencil comparisons and writes mask permitted pixels; they do not compute portal viewpoints automatically.
Phil Fortier describes same apparent-size placement and many rays sampling visible surfaces. Own ratio example and placement diagrams are teaching models.
Direct developer reporting introduces stacked past/present maps only; source has 25-word extraction limit. All 10-unit transforms, state and occupancy examples are original.
Only public talk metadata used: falling-sand scaling and rigid body integration. Tile update algorithm, conflict rules and diagrams are authored, not claimed as full-talk reproduction.
Direct interviews with Alex Beachum and Logan Ver Hoef about small-planet gravity design. Normalized q-family examples are original and not asserted as exact product equations.
Original Wube developer describes relative item distances and terminal gaps. Width-2 length-20 trace is a separate teaching example.
Developer published source defines normalHitbox 8x11 and normalHurtbox 8x9 with same offsets, and assigns Collider separately from hurtbox. Other-state values are distinct.
